triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a rename/interface generalization and could not: the exemplar flags are split one-to-many across rules (entry_is_line_a becomes entry_is_china_301_list123 in china_section_301_component_rate but entry_is_section_122_exempt in section_122_component_rate; entry_is_line_b becomes entry_is_section_232_aluminum, entry_is_china_301_2024_action, and entry_is_section_232_covered in three different rules), so the pre-fix §122 gate cannot be the same predicate under a new name — the denoted condition changes. The rule's own unchanged proof atoms on versions[1] state the §122 exceptions as "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"; the pre-fix formula instead zeroed the surcharge on the witness's China-301-list and aluminum-membership exemplar flags, a condition with no basis in the cited §122 source, and the fix re-grounds it on inputs named for the cited exceptions — squarely untraceable_branch. The "new coverage the module never claimed" escape does not apply: the summary disclaims only special-subcolumn selection and non-ad-valorem duty application, the composition is chapter-wide, and the PR reports round-2 evaluation finding the old gate "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins," i.e. wrong emitted values, not a widened surface.
